engine.title: The multibagger screen qualified nobody for four weeks
engine.body: Corrects what this entry said on 2026-08-27. It read ‘the scan is running on schedule’ and blamed the fixed list on cadence. The ledger says otherwise: the last multibagger row is 2026-08-01, while magic, magicmagic and ai_longterm — the same Saturday job, the same slot — all logged 2026-08-22. Twenty-six days, three Saturdays, nothing written.
engine.note: The screen is not broken. Run on 2026-08-27 it took 11 candidates and rejected 10 for R:R below 2.0 — CHENNPETRO 1.29, FLUOROCHEM 1.07, GLAXO 0.59, which needs a 63% win rate merely to break even. The defect was that a week qualifying nobody wrote nothing at all, so the page served the 1 August list as though it were current. The attempt is recorded either way now. The gate is NOT loosened: publishing a 0.59 R:R to keep the section busy is the exact trade this screen exists to refuse, and an empty week is a real result.

engine.title: Stop buying strength that has already run
engine.body: The 4H RSI ceiling for longs was 75. Splitting every closed trade by the RSI recorded at entry showed the engine bleeding above 65 and profitable below it. The ceiling is now 65.
engine.note: Holds in both halves of the sample and at every cut point tested (60, 65, 70), so it is not one lucky threshold. The threshold was still chosen from this sample, so treat the size as an upper bound.

engine.title: A break-even stop would not have helped
engine.body: The median losing trade was +1.44R in profit before it reversed, and 59% touched a full +1R first. That looks like an obvious fix: move the stop to entry once price pays 1R. Re-walking every trade bar by bar, with winners subject to the same rule, says otherwise.
engine.note: The first version of this test only altered losers, which guarantees a positive answer. Correcting it reversed the conclusion. Nothing tested cleared one standard error, so no stop rule was adopted.

engine.title: Trades were being closed at prices that never traded
engine.body: The grader had never resolved a single trade — an exception was being swallowed silently — leaving a fallback path that could book an exit at a bar from before the signal existed. Every closed trade was re-graded against bars that actually printed.
evidence: exits corrected to a real price
engine.note: This moved the headline number against me. It is published anyway, because the earlier number was not real. Pre-correction data is kept in the repo rather than deleted.

engine.title: A first target must pay back the risk
engine.body: T1 was whichever structural level sat nearest the entry, with no distance test. One signal shipped a T1 worth 0.19R against its own stop, printed beside an R:R of 2.41 quoted off T2. T1 must now return at least 1R.

chess.title: Middlegame: Piece Coordination
chess.body: Good chess is about all your pieces working together. Ask: which of my pieces is worst placed? Improve it. A knight on the rim is dim (a1, h1 etc). A bishop blocked by its own pawns is a 'tall pawn.' Rooks need open files. Queen needs safety. Coordinate: every piece pointing at the same sector = overwhelming attack.

wisdom.title: Simplicity is the Path to Happiness
wisdom.body: Happiness research consistently shows: strong relationships + meaningful work + enough (not excessive) money = high life satisfaction. You're already building all three. Don't confuse complexity for progress. The man who simplifies wins. Less decisions, less noise, less comparison.

book.author: Jim Collins
book.chapter: The Hedgehog Concept: Do One Thing Brilliantly
book.lesson: The fox knows many things. The hedgehog knows one big thing. Collins studied 1,435 Fortune 500 companies over 40 years to find which ones went from good to great. The great ones were all hedgehogs: they found the intersection of three circles — what they are deeply passionate about, what they can be the best in the world at, and what drives their economic engine. They focused there relentlessly and ignored everything else. Good-to-great companies didn't diversify into new businesses. They went deeper into their hedgehog concept until they dominated it.
book.key_quote: Greatness comes from doing one thing so well that the world cannot ignore you.
book.action: Draw your three circles: Passion / Best-in-world potential / Economic driver. Where they overlap is your hedgehog. Do you spend most of your time there?
crux: Good is the enemy of great. Most organisations never become great because they become good enough.
Level 5 Leadership: extreme personal humility combined with intense professional will.
First Who, Then What. Get the right people on the bus before setting direction.
Confront the brutal facts while never losing faith — the Stockdale Paradox.
The Hedgehog Concept: the intersection of what you're deeply passionate about, what you can be best in the world at, and what drives your economics.
One economic denominator — profit per X — clarifies the entire business.
A culture of discipline, not a tyrant imposing discipline.
Technology accelerates momentum; it never creates it.
The Flywheel: relentless pushing in a consistent direction until momentum compounds.
The Doom Loop is the opposite — new programmes, new directions, no accumulation.
Great companies had no miracle moment. Transformation looked dramatic only from outside.
Stop-doing lists matter more than to-do lists.
Compensation gets the right people on the bus; it does not motivate the wrong ones.
learnings: Who beats what. Wrong people make the right strategy fail.
Facing bad news early is a competitive advantage.
Momentum accumulates from consistent direction, not from bursts of intensity.
Greatness is mostly a series of unglamorous, consistent decisions.
examples: Walgreens beat the market 15x from 1975–2000 by fixating on profit per customer visit — one metric, relentlessly.
Darwin Smith at Kimberly-Clark sold the paper mills — the company's historic core — to enter consumer paper against P&G. Shareholder returns beat the market 4x.
Nucor's flywheel: mini-mill technology → lower cost → market share → more mills. Same push for decades.
adapt: Hedgehog: CA precision + FP&A + building with AI. That intersection is narrower and stronger than 'finance content'.
Economic denominator for Codex: profit per customer, not downloads.
Brutal fact: 1H signals have no measurable edge. Faith: the daily equity engine does. Hold both.
Stop-doing list beats the roadmap. Deleting three TradeFlow pages was the flywheel push.

minimalism.title: The Empty Surface
minimalism.body: Keep one surface in your home completely empty. A desk, a counter, a shelf. It becomes a visual reference point — the moment things start accumulating elsewhere, you notice.
minimalism.action: Clear one surface fully. Keep it clear for a week.
minimalism.label: Minimalism

etiquette.title: Dress One Notch Above The Room
etiquette.body: Not two — two reads as trying. One notch signals you took the occasion seriously. In the Gulf, conservative beats fashionable in every professional setting.
etiquette.action: Check tomorrow's outfit against the room you will be in.
etiquette.label: Etiquette

stillness.title: Silence Is A Position
stillness.body: You are not required to have an opinion on everything you encounter. 'I don't know enough about that' is a complete and unusually strong answer.
stillness.action: Decline to have an opinion on one thing today.
stillness.label: Stillness

model.title: Inversion
model.body: Solve the problem backwards. Instead of 'how do I succeed?', ask 'how would I guarantee failure?' — then avoid that. The failure list is concrete and short; the success list is vague and infinite.
model.action: Invert your biggest current goal. Write the three surest ways to fail it.
model.label: Mental Model

arabic.label: Arabic

drill.title: Name The Assumption
drill.body: Every model rests on two or three assumptions doing all the work. Find them. The rest is arithmetic and does not deserve your review time.
drill.action: Find the two assumptions carrying your current model.
drill.label: Drill

health.title: Strength Is Longevity, Not Vanity
health.body: Muscle mass and grip strength both independently predict lifespan. After 30 you lose 3–8% of muscle per decade unless you resist it, and the decline accelerates. Sarcopenia is what puts people in care homes.
health.action: Two sets of a compound lift. Squat, hinge, push, or pull.
health.label: Health

quote.name: Melinda Gates
quote.quote: A woman with a voice is by definition a strong woman.

lesson.lesson: Waste no more time arguing about what a good man should be. Be one.

case.title: Razorpay: B2B Sales Playbook
case.story: Razorpay started with a landing page and no product. Collected emails. Launched 3 months later. Grew from $0 to $7.5B valuation by making checkout dead simple for developers.
case.lesson: Validate before you build. A landing page with a waitlist tells you more than 3 months of product development.

fpna.title: Sensitivity Analysis
fpna.body: Which assumption, if wrong, blows up your model? Identify it. Test it. Present the range.

cfo.title: Dubai FC Reality
cfo.body: AED 30K+ FC roles at ADNOC, Emirates, MAF, DP World: they want Big 4 background OR 8+ years in a listed company + CA/ACCA + ERP experience. Your edge: FP&A depth + IFRS knowledge + Power BI automation. Highlight cost savings you drove.

money_hack.title: Direct Funds Only
money_hack.body: Regular mutual funds cost 1–1.5% more per year. Over 20 years = 30% of corpus gone.

dubai.title: The package is not the salary
dubai.body: Gulf offers split into basic, housing, transport and a school allowance. Gratuity accrues on BASIC only — 21 days' basic per year for the first five. An offer that is 40% basic and 60% allowances quietly halves your end-of-service.
dubai.targets: Ask for the split in writing before you counter.
dubai.action: Push basic up, not total up. Same headline number, materially more gratuity.

desk.productivity: Weekly review: 15 min every Sunday. What worked, what's next week's #1.

father.title: Take a photo of the ordinary
father.do: Photograph something unremarkable — her on the floor, mid-task — rather than a milestone.
father.why: You will have hundreds of milestone photos and almost none of the texture of daily life at seven months, which is what you will actually want later.

father.title: Say goodbye properly
father.do: Never slip out unseen. Say you are leaving, say you will be back, then go — even if she cries.
father.why: Disappearing without warning teaches vigilance. A predictable goodbye, repeated, teaches that departures end in returns. The crying is not the failure; it is the process.

life_wisdom.translation: Non-violence in thought, word and act
life_wisdom.teaching: The most demanding version is not physical — it is refusing to injure with speech or intent, including toward yourself.
life_wisdom.apply: Notice the sentence you would not say to a colleague, then check whether you say it to yourself about your own work. The standard should be the same.

life_wisdom.teaching: The second element of the path, sitting between right view and right speech — the resolve that shapes what follows.
life_wisdom.apply: Before a difficult conversation, name your intention in one sentence. If it is 'to be proved right', the conversation will fail regardless of your evidence.

speaking.title: Present standing
speaking.drill: Deliver a two-minute update standing up, even alone at your desk.
speaking.why: Posture changes breath, breath changes voice. It transfers to seated delivery after about a week.

interview_tech.q: How would you decide between renting and buying a distribution centre?
interview_tech.a: Compare NPV of both over the same horizon at the same discount rate. Rent is an operating commitment — now on balance sheet under IFRS 16 anyway — with flexibility to exit. Buying ties up capital and carries residual value risk, but fixes occupancy cost and creates an asset. The real question is strategic, not arithmetic: how confident are you in the network design over 15 years. If the answer is 'not very', pay the premium for optionality.

interview_tech.q: Your group operates in a country that introduces 15% VAT. What breaks?
interview_tech.a: Systems and margin, in that order. Systems: tax codes on every SKU, correct treatment of zero-rated versus exempt lines, input recovery on mixed-use costs, and the reverse charge on imported services — all of which must be in the ERP before go-live, not after. Margin: if you absorb VAT rather than pass it through, gross margin falls by roughly the VAT rate on the absorbed portion. Cash: output VAT is collected before it is remitted, so there is a temporary working capital benefit that people mistake for profit.

interview_soft.a: They are screening for whether you have thought about it or are just leaving somewhere. Be concrete: the Gulf retail market's scale and the concentration of regional HQs; UAE corporate tax making the finance function genuinely more technical than it was; and the specific fit between your multi-country consolidation experience and a group operating across GCC markets. Do not lead with tax-free income or lifestyle — every candidate says it and none of it is about the job.

interview_soft.q: How do you prioritise when everything is urgent?
interview_soft.a: Give a working rule, not a philosophy. Something like: anything with a statutory deadline is non-negotiable; then anything that changes a decision being made this week; then anything that compounds — process fixes that stop the same fire recurring; then everything else. The part interviewers actually want: what you stopped doing and who you told. Prioritisation without explicit de-prioritisation is just a longer list.
